rv.q: Ten years on, Mamma Mia! – a love story set to Abba songs – still doesn't rival Sophocles, but it remains as stonkingly, wonderfully, unbelievably good as the first time I saw it.
Just give it a chance – it’ll make you smile.
They are timeless feel-good songs that, as my night at the taverna shows, make you want to sing and dance.
That, I think, would be overstating the charms of this skilful, good-spirited, thoroughly enjoyable but knowingly disposable evening.
It shouldn’t work: Mamma Mia! The Party fails as a musical, a gig, a dining experience and a nightclub.

The plot is cheesier than a truckload of feta. Kate (Steph Parry) runs the taverna with her Greek husband, whom she met while filming Mamma Mia! But now Nikos (Fed Zanni) is reluctant to let her nephew be with his daughter.
The mixture of Abba songs, camp dance routines, platform boots and Lycra costumes based around a soppy romance comedy script creates a delightful evening of sheer fun and pleasure.
I had fun, but I couldn’t get that price tag out of my head: you’re effectively paying for an expensive simulation of a cheap night out.

“Some of the songs are oddly static, but when the choreography does get going it's terrific...The current cast appear to have been chosen more for their singing voices than their serious acting ability.
I do understand why the show has done so well, but in my opinion if Mamma Mia! had just premiered today against its current competitors, I would give it a lifetime of 6 months and no more.
It defies intellectualising with a playfully bacchic twirl and a great big grin.
But it’s a case of Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! your Money, Money, Money.
The actors looked like they were having a blast and that enjoyment was completely contagious.
